blurb: Planets, rockets and astronauts: jokes that are out of this world

questions.q: How do you throw a party in outer space?
questions.fact: Bonus: How do you put a baby astronaut to sleep? You rock-et.
questions.src: classic

questions.q: What did Mars say to Saturn?
questions.fact: Bonus: Where do astronauts keep their sandwiches? In a launch box.
questions.src: classic; premise: Saturn has rings; checker: 'See you next orbit' was a space pun and 'Stay warm out there' leaned on Saturn's cold, both swapped for flat sign-offs

questions.q: How does the moon cut its hair?
questions.fact: Bonus: How does the solar system hold up its pants? With an asteroid belt.
questions.src: classic; premise: the asteroid belt lies between Mars and Jupiter; checker: 'It lets it grow out' could read as the waxing moon, swapped

questions.q: What do you call a magician in outer space?
questions.fact: Bonus: What did the astronaut spot in the frying pan? An unidentified frying object.
questions.src: classic (flying saucer / sorcerer); distractors are puns on the wrong jobs

questions.q: What kind of star wears sunglasses?
questions.fact: Bonus: Why did the moon skip dessert? It was already full.
questions.src: classic

questions.q: The moon has looked gloomy lately. Don't worry, it's just going through ___
questions.fact: Bonus: What's an astronaut's favorite key on the keyboard? The space bar.
questions.src: classic; premise: the moon goes through phases

questions.q: Why didn't the sun go to college?
options: It had no time to study
questions.fact: Bonus: What did the sun say when it met Earth? Nice to heat you.
questions.src: classic; premise: the sun's core is about 15 million degrees C (NASA)

questions.q: How can you tell the moon is running low on money?
options: It's down to its last quarter
questions.fact: The pun: a quarter is a coin, and the last quarter is a real moon phase, when half of the moon's face is lit.
questions.src: classic; premise: last (third) quarter moon phase shows half the disk lit; checker: 'hiding behind clouds' could read as dodging bills, swapped for a flat literal

questions.q: Did you hear about the new restaurant on the moon? Great food, but ___
questions.fact: Bonus: Why did the astronaut get in trouble in class? He kept spacing out.
questions.src: classic; premise: the moon has almost no atmosphere

questions.q: Why haven't aliens ever visited our solar system?
options: It's too far off the map
questions.fact: Bonus: What do planets like to read? Comet books.
questions.src: classic; premise: our solar system has one star, the Sun

questions.q: The satellites held an awards night. The speeches ran long, but ___
questions.fact: Bonus: Why did the star win an award? It was a shining example.
questions.src: classic, adapted from the folk joke about two antennas (or satellites) whose wedding reception was excellent; premise: satellites receive and relay signals

questions.q: My parents always said the sky's the limit. That's why I never became ___
questions.fact: Bonus: Why did the rocket go to the party? It wanted to have a blast.
questions.src: classic, adapted

blurb: Rain, wind, clouds and storms: today's forecast calls for groans

questions.q: Why did the weather reporter bring a bar of soap to work?
questions.fact: Bonus: What did the cloud say when it couldn't make it to the party? Can I take a rain check?
questions.src: classic

questions.q: How does a hurricane see where it's going?
questions.fact: Bonus: Why was the thunder upset with the lightning? The lightning always got there first and stole its thunder.
questions.src: classic; premise: a hurricane has an eye; light travels faster than sound, so lightning is seen before thunder is heard

questions.q: What does a cloud wear under its raincoat?
questions.fact: Bonus: What did the puddle say to the rain? Drop in anytime!
questions.src: classic

questions.q: What's worse than when it's raining cats and dogs?
questions.fact: The pun: you 'hail' a taxi by waving one down, and hail is also the balls of ice that fall in a storm.
questions.src: classic (in print since at least 1911, no known author, per Barry Popik); replaced 'Fowl weather', which shared its fowl/foul pun with Turkey Talk's 'fowl language'

questions.q: Why don't people trust clouds?
questions.fact: Bonus: What do clouds wear in their hair? Rainbows.
questions.src: classic

questions.q: Why does the cloud never spend its allowance?
options: It's saving for a rainy day
questions.fact: Bonus: What's the difference between weather and climate? You can't weather a tree, but you can climate.
questions.src: classic; bonus is the classic weather/climate (climb it) joke

questions.q: Why does lightning never need to borrow a phone charger?
questions.fact: Bonus: What's the opposite of a cold front? A warm back.
questions.src: original; premise: lightning is a discharge of built-up electric charge; checker: 'outlet' distractor echoed Road Trip's keyed 'outlet' punchline, swapped

questions.q: What did one raindrop say to the other?
options: Two heads are better than one
questions.fact: Bonus: What kind of dance does a tornado do best? The twist.
questions.src: classic (two's company, three's a crowd)

questions.q: I'd tell you a joke about the wind, but ___
questions.fact: Bonus: Why did the cloud get kicked out of the group chat? It kept raining on everyone's parade.
questions.src: original

questions.q: The forecast says a 50 percent chance of rain, so today I'm carrying ___
questions.fact: Bonus: Why did Dad stand outside holding his wallet wide open? He heard there'd be some change in the weather.
questions.src: classic

questions.q: I tried to catch some fog this morning, but ___
questions.fact: Bonus: What does a cloud do when it's itchy? It finds the nearest skyscraper.
questions.src: classic

questions.q: What happens when the fog finally lifts in Los Angeles?
questions.fact: The pun: when the fog lifts, 'you see LA,' which sounds just like UCLA, the big university in Los Angeles.
questions.src: classic; premise: UCLA is the University of California, Los Angeles; LA gets coastal fog

blurb: Books, readers and libraries: jokes with a strong spine

questions.q: Where do books sleep?
questions.fact: Bonus: Why are bookends such good friends? They always support each other.
questions.src: classic

questions.q: Why did the library book go to the doctor?
options: It had a really bad cough
It needed to be checked out
questions.fact: Bonus: Why did the writer shut the window? There was a draft.
questions.src: classic

questions.q: Why was the book always so cold?
questions.fact: Bonus: Why is a bookmark such a loyal friend? It always saves your place.
questions.src: classic; premise: hardcover books wear paper dust jackets

questions.q: What do librarians take with them when they go fishing?
questions.fact: Bonus: Which section of the library is the most slippery? Non-friction.
questions.src: classic; premise: a bookworm is a keen reader, and worms are fishing bait; replaced 'ashamed of our shelves', the deck's third shelf/self pun

questions.q: Why are libraries the tallest buildings in town?
questions.fact: Bonus: Why did the reader buy a brighter lamp? She wanted to do some light reading.
questions.src: classic

questions.q: What do you call a photo a book takes of itself?
questions.fact: Bonus: Why did the old library book look like a puppy? It was dog-eared.
questions.src: classic; premise: dog-eared means page corners folded down

questions.q: I just started a book about mazes, and ___
options: I lent it to a friend
questions.fact: Bonus: What's a librarian's favorite vegetable? Quiet peas.
questions.src: classic

questions.q: I'm reading a book about teleportation. ___
options: It's bound to take me places
questions.fact: The pun: a book is 'bound' when its pages are sewn or glued into a cover, and 'bound to' also means 'sure to.'
questions.src: classic

questions.q: They say never judge a book by its cover. That's why I always ___
questions.fact: Bonus: What kind of stories do giraffes tell? Tall tales.
questions.src: classic, adapted

questions.q: My e-reader's battery died on the last page of a mystery novel. ___
questions.fact: Bonus: Why do books love autumn? They get to turn over a new leaf.
questions.src: original; premise: a leaf is also a page of a book

questions.q: I asked the library for a book on patience. They told me ___
questions.fact: Bonus: Why did the library book finally say sorry? The apology was long overdue.
questions.src: original

questions.q: Why is the self-help shelf at my library always empty?
questions.fact: Bonus: Why did the book join a gym? It wanted a stronger spine.
questions.src: original; checker: 'checked out' was the deck's $200 punchline, swapped

blurb: Cars, trains, planes and vacations: jokes for the long drive

questions.q: How do trains eat their food?
questions.fact: Bonus: Why was the old car so sleepy? It was totally exhausted.
questions.src: classic

questions.q: Why couldn't the bicycle stand up on its own?
questions.fact: Bonus: What did the traffic light say to the car? Don't look, I'm changing.
questions.src: classic

questions.q: Why did the car get a flat tire?
options: There was a fork in the road
questions.fact: Bonus: Why is camping so tiring? It's in-tents.
questions.src: classic

questions.q: What did the jack say to the car?
options: Can I give you a lift?
questions.fact: Bonus: Where do pencils go on vacation? Pencil-vania.
questions.src: classic; premise: a jack lifts a car so a tire can be changed; replaced the frog 'toad away' joke (frogs are Animal Crackers' lane and a likely repeat)

questions.q: Where do cars go swimming?
questions.fact: Bonus: Why did the old road map have so many fans? It was a legend.
questions.src: classic; premise: a map's legend is its key

questions.q: Why was the train late?
questions.fact: Bonus: Why did the highway get a promotion? It always went the extra mile.
questions.src: classic

questions.q: Why did the car apply for a new job?
options: It wanted to be more driven
questions.fact: Bonus: Why is the suitcase so convincing? It always makes a strong case.
questions.src: classic

questions.q: Why did the airplane get sent to its room?
questions.fact: Bonus: Why did my phone love the long flight? It got to relax in airplane mode all day.
questions.src: classic

questions.q: What has four wheels and flies?
questions.fact: Bonus: Why is a bicycle bad at keeping promises? It always backpedals.
questions.src: classic; checker: 'A small airplane' and 'A flying car' really do have four wheels and fly, replaced with vehicles that do neither

questions.q: I couldn't figure out how my seatbelt worked. Then ___
questions.fact: Bonus: How is the pilot's new business going? It really took off.
questions.src: classic

questions.q: Paper road maps tell you everything you need to know, except ___
options: how to fold them back up
questions.fact: Bonus: What's a highway's favorite fruit spread? Traffic jam.
questions.src: classic folk observation

questions.q: I went on vacation to unplug from everything. I spent the whole trip ___
questions.fact: Bonus: What do you get when you put a car in the oven? A hot rod.
questions.src: original

blurb: Fish, whales, crabs and waves: jokes that make a big splash

questions.q: Why don't oysters share their pearls?
questions.fact: Bonus: Why are fish so smart? They live in schools.
questions.src: classic (reserved for this deck); premise: oysters make pearls

questions.q: What do you call a fish wearing a bow tie?
questions.fact: Bonus: How does a clam call its friends? On its shell phone.
questions.src: classic

questions.q: How do you make a squid laugh?
questions.fact: Bonus: Why did the whale go to the party? It wanted to have a whale of a time.
questions.src: classic; premise: a squid has ten limbs, eight arms plus two tentacles

questions.q: What do you call a fish that performs surgery?
questions.fact: Bonus: What part of a fish weighs the most? The scales.
questions.src: classic; premise: the sturgeon is a real fish; distractors are puns on the wrong jobs

questions.q: What kind of hair do oceans have?
questions.fact: Bonus: What did one fish say to the other after a year apart? Long time, no sea.
questions.src: classic

questions.q: Why won't fish ever go on the internet?
questions.fact: Bonus: Why did the family buy the boat? It was for sail.
questions.src: classic

questions.q: What's the best way to talk to a fish?
questions.fact: Bonus: What kind of fish only comes out at night? A starfish.
questions.src: classic

questions.q: What does an octopus wear on a cold day?
questions.fact: The pun: a coat of arms is a family crest from the days of knights, and an octopus has eight arms to keep warm.
questions.src: classic; premise: octopuses have eight arms

questions.q: Why do fish live in salt water?
questions.fact: Bonus: How do little fish get to school? They ride the octobus.
questions.src: classic

questions.q: Two fish are in a tank. One turns to the other and says ___
options: I think we need more water
Do you know how to drive this?
questions.fact: Bonus: What do you get when you cross a fish with an elephant? Swimming trunks.
questions.src: classic

questions.q: Why is the ocean so salty?
questions.fact: The pun: 'salty' also means grumpy, and waves are the sea's hello. The real salt comes mostly from rocks, carried in by rivers.
questions.src: classic; premise: sea salt is mostly minerals weathered from rock and carried by rivers (NOAA)

questions.q: Everyone thinks a pirate's favorite letter is R, but his real favorite is ___
questions.fact: Bonus: Where do fish go on vacation? Finland.
questions.src: classic pirate joke (you'd think it's R, but it's the C / sea); replaced the seagull 'bagels' joke (bread is Rise and Shine's lane, and its flying bagel echoed Rise and Shine's 'plain bagel')

blurb: Dinosaurs and fossils: jokes from way, way, way back

questions.q: What do you call a sleeping dinosaur?
questions.fact: Bonus: What do you get when you cross a dinosaur with fireworks? Dino-mite!
questions.src: classic (reserved for this deck)

questions.q: What do you call a dinosaur that knows lots of big words?
questions.fact: Bonus: Which dinosaur is the best at cleaning the house? The Tricera-mops.
questions.src: classic

questions.q: What did the dinosaur put on its kitchen floor?
questions.fact: Bonus: What do you call a dinosaur that never gives up? A Try-and-try-and-try-ceratops.
questions.src: classic; premise: dinosaurs are reptiles

questions.q: How do you ask a dinosaur if it wants a hot drink?
questions.fact: The pun: 'Tea, Rex?' sounds like T. rex, short for Tyrannosaurus rex, a name that means 'tyrant lizard king.'
questions.src: classic; premise: Tyrannosaurus rex means tyrant lizard king

questions.q: Why was the fossil so famous?
questions.fact: Bonus: What do you call a dinosaur that's great at hide-and-seek? Do-you-think-he-saw-us.
questions.src: original; premise: fossils are preserved in rock

questions.q: Why do paleontologists love their jobs?
questions.fact: Bonus: What did the paleontologist say to the messy fossil? I have a bone to pick with you.
questions.src: classic; premise: paleontologists dig up fossils

questions.q: What kind of dinosaur can you ride in a rodeo?
questions.fact: Bonus: What do dinosaurs use to pay their bills? Tyrannosaurus checks.
questions.src: classic (Brontosaurus / bronco); checker: distractors are now coined dino puns that don't connect to a rodeo, so it isn't a spot-the-misspelling

questions.q: Why did the dinosaur eat the whole factory?
questions.fact: Bonus: Why did the T. rex lose the arm-wrestling match? It came up a little short.
questions.src: classic; premise: many dinosaurs were plant-eaters; T. rex had very short arms

questions.q: What makes more noise than a dinosaur?
questions.fact: Bonus: Why do museums keep showing old dinosaur bones? They can't afford new ones.
questions.src: classic

questions.q: Why did the dinosaur cross the road?
questions.fact: Bonus: Why did the Stegosaurus offer to set the table? It already had the plates.
questions.src: classic; premise: chickens appeared tens of millions of years after the non-bird dinosaurs; Stegosaurus had bony back plates

questions.q: How should you start a conversation with a T. rex?
questions.fact: Bonus: Why shouldn't you race a velociraptor for the last cookie? Its name means 'swift thief.'
questions.src: classic; checker reworded the setup so it doesn't echo Under the Sea's 'best way to talk to a fish'; premise: Velociraptor means swift seizer or swift thief

questions.q: The museum guide said the dinosaur skeleton is 70 million and 3 years old. Why the 3?
questions.fact: Bonus: Why did the dinosaur buy a new phone? Its old one was a total fossil.
questions.src: classic; premise: many dinosaur fossils are around 66 to 70+ million years old
